messages.content: Thank you for taking the time to meet with me today. To start, I would like to understand the high-level goals you have for enhancing the university student portal. What are the primary objectives you hope to achieve with the new features of personalised timetable management, automated grade notifications, and a structured module feedback system?

Thanks for having me! So, I guess the main thing I want is to make the timetable easier to read and use. It's kind of a mess right now, and I think it would be great if we could, like, colour-code things or hide classes that don’t happen. That would really help.

Also, getting notifications when grades come out would be super handy. I mean, it’s always a bit stressful waiting for those, right? Just a little ping when they’re up would be nice.

And, I really think there should be a way for us to give feedback on the modules we take. It would be nice to share what works and what doesn’t after the teaching ends. So, yeah, those are the main things I’m hoping for!

Thank you for sharing those insights! To clarify and ensure I fully understand your needs, let’s break down each of the points you've mentioned.

Starting with the personalised timetable management, you mentioned wanting it to be easier to read and use. You suggested colour-coding and the option to hide classes that don’t occur. Can you elaborate on how you envision the colour-coding system working? What specific categories or types of classes would you want to differentiate using colours?

Oh, um, I guess I haven't really thought about the specific colours or categories too much. But I think it would be helpful if, like, different modules could have different colours. Maybe something for lectures, something else for tutorials, and then, like, a different colour for study blocks or personal time? Just something that makes it all pop and easier to see at a glance, you know? It would just help me not to mix things up. Does that make sense?

That makes perfect sense. So, if I understand correctly, you would like the timetable to feature a colour-coding system that differentiates between various types of activities, such as lectures, tutorials, and personal study time. This would help you visually identify your schedule at a glance and prevent any mix-ups. 

Now, moving on to the automated grade notifications, you mentioned that receiving a notification when grades are posted would alleviate some stress. Could you clarify what type of notification you would prefer? For instance, would you like a pop-up notification within the portal, an email alert, or perhaps a mobile notification? What specifically would work best for you?

Yeah, that makes sense! For the notifications, I think it would be best to get an email alert. I check my email regularly, so it would be hard to miss. A pop-up in the portal could work too, but I don’t always have it open, you know? So, I’d say an email would be the most reliable for me. Just something simple to let me know when grades are up!

Thank you for that clarification! To summarize, you prefer receiving an email alert when grades are posted, as you check your email regularly. This would ensure that you do not miss any important updates. 

Now, let's discuss the structured module feedback system you mentioned. You expressed the desire for a way to share feedback on the modules after the teaching ends. Can you detail what specific aspects of the modules you would like to provide feedback on? For example, are you thinking about aspects such as teaching quality, course materials, or perhaps the assessment methods? What specific feedback areas should the system focus on?

Sure! I think it would be good to give feedback on a few things. First, the teaching quality is definitely important — like how well the lecturer explains things and engages with us. Then, the course materials should be included too. I mean, if they’re helpful or not, that sort of thing. And I guess it could also be about the assessments, like if they make sense with what we learned or if they’re too hard. Just those kinds of things would be helpful to share!

Thank you for providing those details! To summarize, you would like the structured module feedback system to focus on three main areas: 

1. Teaching quality, including how well lecturers explain concepts and engage with students.
2. Course materials, assessing their helpfulness and relevance.
3. Assessment methods, evaluating whether they align with the learning objectives and their difficulty level.

Now, before we conclude, are there any limitations or restrictions we should be aware of regarding these enhancements? For example, are there specific technical constraints or user accessibility considerations that we need to keep in mind?

Oh, um, I haven’t really thought about any of that stuff. I just know what I want it to do. I guess it’s good to think about it, but I'm not sure if there are any technical issues or anything. I just hope it can all work smoothly with what we already have. But yeah, I can’t really say much about limitations or restrictions. I just want it to be easier to use for everyone!

Thank you for your honesty. To summarize our discussion, you would like the enhancements to focus on:

1. Personalised timetable management with a colour-coding system to differentiate between types of activities, such as lectures, tutorials, and personal study time.
2. Automated grade notifications via email alerts to inform students when grades are posted.
3. A structured module feedback system that allows students to provide feedback on teaching quality, course materials, and assessment methods.

You also expressed a desire for these enhancements to work smoothly with the existing portal infrastructure, but you are unsure about any specific technical limitations.

With this information, we have gathered a solid foundation of clear requirements. Thank you for your participation in this interview. 

REQUIREMENTS_COMPLETE
